Haida

Haida public sources offer distinct routes through governance, living arts and community knowledge. The Council of the Haida Nation explains its Haida Gwaii institutions, while a collaborative museum guide emphasizes named makers and language. A separate Alaska tribal-government history should be read within its own institutional scope.

01

Identity and context

Haida people have homelands in Haida Gwaii and southeastern Alaska, with distinct contemporary communities.

Read the sources [1] Council of the Haida Nation

02

A path for deeper reading

Focus the next stage of research on: Haida-authored history, language revitalization, governance and relationships to land and sea. The sources below are selected reading paths; their authorship, dates and community scope should guide how they are used.

Read the sources [1] Council of the Haida Nation [2] Central Council of the Tlingit and Haida Indian Tribes of Alaska

03

Different institutions within a wider people

The Council of the Haida Nation traces its formation to 1974 and explains relationships among national, hereditary and village institutions. Its account distinguishes Old Massett Village Council and Skidegate Band Council as village governments with community responsibilities. This provides an institutional starting point for Haida Gwaii, while detailed constitutional and community histories require their own review.

Read the sources [1] Council of the Haida Nation

04

Makers, language and the history of collecting

The Canadian Museum of History’s collaborative guide presents Haida making as connected with language, practical knowledge and relationships. It also explains how colonial collecting could separate belongings from named makers and their intended meanings. Haida contributors helped select and review the educational package. The linked objects and recordings need separate reading and reuse checks.

Read the sources [3] Canadian Museum of History, with named Haida collaborators

05

An Alaska institutional reading route

The Central Council of Tlingit and Haida Indian Tribes of Alaska presents a separate history of collective political advocacy and institution-building. Its timeline concerns that tribal government; it does not collapse Tlingit and Haida identities or replace individual community histories.

Read the sources [2] Central Council of the Tlingit and Haida Indian Tribes of Alaska

What needs further research

  • Compare community-authored histories across Haida Gwaii and Alaska without treating one government as every Haida community.
  • Review current constitutional documents and selected maker-led educational works; linked objects and recordings remain separate tasks.

Council of the Haida Nation — origins and institutions ↗

Read the Council’s historical origins and explanations of hereditary, village and national institutions. This is the Council’s own account, not a single governmental model for every Haida community.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Selected complete historical/governance paragraphs, web lines 94–105, 116, 180–189, 257–260. The current officials roster and 2003 constitutional-version wording were not adopted.

Review recorded: October 28, 2026

Access note: Public main body read normally. No original 1974 minutes, election law or current legal interpretation checked. The page contains historical constitutional references; no present officeholders or exact jurisdiction asserted.

https://www.haidanation.ca/about/chn

Indigenous-led / tribal-government historyCentral Council of the Tlingit and Haida Indian Tribes of AlaskaSource 2

History - Tlingit & Haida ↗

The Central Council’s timeline offers an Alaska institutional history involving Tlingit and Haida people. It is complementary to, and distinct from, the Council of the Haida Nation account.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Complete Our History timeline and Generations to Come/mission body, web lines 65–119; leadership biographies and linked laws/cases not separately reviewed.

Review recorded: October 28, 2026

Access note: Public actual HTML body read. This is the Central Council’s institutional history and interpretation, not every Tlingit or Haida community’s government. Underlying statutes, court records, amounts and present rights not independently checked; no demographic totals or ceremonies reproduced.

https://tlingitandhaida.gov/about-us/history/

Haida Arts and Technologies — introduction and acknowledgments ↗

Substantial introduction relates making, language, exchange and colonial collecting. Credits Ariane Xay Kuyaas, Sean Young and Jaskwaan Bedard. Linked objects, lessons and videos were not individually reviewed.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Complete main introductory prose and acknowledgments, ending with thanks to named Haida collaborators; topic tiles read only as navigation.

Review recorded: October 28, 2026

Access note: Web extraction exceeded4MB size limit; normal same-URL HTML 200 retrieved and actual body read. Museum/community-collaborative interpretation, not permission to reproduce objects, motifs, recordings or restricted knowledge. No individual craft instructions copied.
